### S3. Seasonal bootstrap confidence intervals

Per-season von Mises regression estimates with 95% bootstrap
percentile intervals, computed from **season-stratified** (independent
per-season) models.  These CIs differ slightly from those reported in
Table~1 of the main text, which are derived from the **year × season
interaction model** (full model with season-specific slopes from a
single joint fit).  The interaction-model CIs account for the
cross-season covariance structure and are therefore the primary
reference.

| Season | $\beta$ (h/decade) | 95% CI | $\kappa$ | n obs | n years |
|--------|--------------------|----------|----------|-------|---------|
| Spring (MAM) | $-0.0650$ | $(-0.135, 0.008)$ | 2.36 | 3,168 | 35 |
| Summer (JJA) | $0.0195$ | $(-0.046, 0.079)$ | 2.72 | 3,111 | 35 |
| Autumn (SON) | $0.0850$ | $(-0.007, 0.162)$ | 2.37 | 3,002 | 35 |
| Winter (DJF) | $-0.1886$ | $(-0.283, -0.037)$ | 2.61 | 2,882 | 35 |

### S5. Power analysis

The power analysis (see `notebooks/02-power-analysis.qmd`
for full details) estimated a minimum detectable effect of
25--30 min/decade at $80\%$ power for the full record
($\kappa \approx 2.5$). Seasonal sub-analyses require effects
45--60 min/decade to achieve the same power.

![Power curves for the full record, single-season, and half-season
  sample sizes at the observed concentration
  $\kappa \approx 2.5$.](../results/figures/power_curve.pdf)

![Sensitivity of detection power to the concentration parameter
  $\kappa$.](../results/figures/power_curve_kappa_sensitivity.pdf)

### S6. Supplementary analysis: temperature-weighted regression

Temperature-weighted von Mises regression (weight = diurnal amplitude)
yielded $+0.0210$ h/decade (95% CI: $-0.0125$, $+0.0528$). The sign
differs from the unweighted pooled estimate ($-0.0281$), but both values
are near zero and well within each other's confidence intervals,
confirming this is sampling noise around a null result rather than a
substantive discrepancy.

### S7. Mardia circular--linear rank correlation

Non-parametric test using all daily observations:

- $\rho_c$ = 0.0252
- Bootstrap p-value = 0.0206
- n = 12,163

The small but statistically significant correlation is consistent with
a weak association between year and peak hour, in line with the small
effect size estimated by the pooled MLE model.

### S8. Per-season temperature-weighted regression

Temperature-weighted von Mises regression (weight = diurnal amplitude),
estimated per season and for all observations pooled.

| Season | $\beta$ (h/decade) | $\kappa$ | n obs |
|--------|-------------------:|:--------:|:-----:|
| Spring (MAM) | $-0.0278$ | 4.35 | 3,168 |
| Summer (JJA) | $+0.0538$ | 5.79 | 3,111 |
| Autumn (SON) | $+0.1134$ | 3.51 | 3,002 |
| Winter (DJF) | $-0.0866$ | 1.77 | 2,882 |
| Pooled | $+0.0210$ | 3.42 | 12,163 |

The seasonal pattern maintains the same directional sign as the unweighted
primary analysis for all four seasons, but the magnitudes differ in a
mechanistically informative way. The winter advance shrinks from
$-0.19$ to $-0.09$ h/decade ($\Delta = +0.10$) when high-amplitude
days are up-weighted, indicating the winter peak-hour advance is
concentrated on low-amplitude (cloudy, advection-dominated) days.
Autumn and summer shift slightly more positive ($\Delta \approx +0.03$
each), suggesting the weak delay is subtly enhanced on high-amplitude
days. Spring remains near zero under both schemes.

### S9. Per-season Mardia circular--linear rank correlation

Non-parametric rank correlation (Mardia 1976) between peak hour and
year, computed per season.

| Season | $\rho_c$ | n obs |
|--------|---------:|:-----:|
| Spring (MAM) | 0.0447 | 3,168 |
| Summer (JJA) | 0.0395 | 3,111 |
| Autumn (SON) | 0.0579 | 3,002 |
| Winter (DJF) | 0.0573 | 2,882 |
| Pooled | $0.0252$ | 12,163 |

All four seasonal $\rho_c$ values are in a narrow range (0.04--0.06),
indicating that the weak but statistically significant pooled
correlation is not driven by any single season.

### S10. Autocorrelation diagnostic

Lag-1 through lag-7 autocorrelation of daily peak-hour values, computed
per season and for all observations pooled (sorted chronologically).

| Season | AC(1) | AC(2) | AC(3) | AC(4) | AC(5) | AC(6) | AC(7) |
|--------|:-----:|:-----:|:-----:|:-----:|:-----:|:-----:|:-----:|
| Spring | --0.019 | --0.044 | --0.021 | 0.016 | 0.020 | 0.028 | 0.004 |
| Summer | 0.002 | 0.006 | --0.018 | 0.004 | --0.024 | 0.006 | --0.026 |
| Autumn | 0.019 | 0.018 | 0.021 | 0.028 | 0.039 | 0.042 | 0.002 |
| Winter | --0.034 | --0.047 | --0.036 | --0.059 | 0.008 | --0.017 | 0.020 |
| Pooled | 0.026 | 0.018 | 0.028 | 0.031 | 0.056 | 0.054 | 0.055 |

All autocorrelation values are within $\pm 0.06$, confirming that
short-range serial dependence in peak hours is negligible. The i.i.d.\
bootstrap used throughout this study is therefore adequate for
inference.

### S11. Contingency analysis

The primary MLE converged successfully; no fallback was required.
